In [[mathematics]], especially [[category theory]], the '''core''' of a [[category (mathematics)|category]] ''C'' is the category whose objects are the objects of ''C'' and whose morphisms are the invertible morphisms in ''C''.<ref name=Gabriel>Pierre Gabriel, Michel Zisman, § 1.5.4., Calculus of fractions and homotopy theory, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete, Band 35, Springer (1967) [https://people.math.rochester.edu/faculty/doug/otherpapers/GZ.pdf]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Construction 1.3.5.4.  |url=https://kerodon.net/tag/007G |website=Kerodon}}</ref><ref>{{nlab|id=core+groupoid|title=core groupoid}}</ref> In other words, it is the largest [[groupoid]] [[subcategory]].

As a [[functor]] <math>C \mapsto \operatorname{core}(C)</math>, the core is a [[right adjoint]] to the inclusion of the category of (small) groupoids into the category of (small) categories.<ref name=Gabriel /> On the other hand, the left adjoint to the above inclusion is the [[fundamental groupoid functor]].

For [[∞-category|∞-categories]], <math>\operatorname{core}</math> is defined as a right adjoint to the inclusion ∞-Grpd <math>\hookrightarrow</math> ∞-Cat.<ref>§ 3.5.2. and Corollary 3.5.3. of {{cite book |last=Cisinski |first=Denis-Charles |author-link=Denis-Charles Cisinski |url=https://cisinski.app.uni-regensburg.de/CatLR.pdf |title=Higher Categories and Homotopical Algebra |date=2023|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |isbn=978-1108473200 |location= |language=en |authorlink=}}</ref> The core of an ∞-category <math>C</math> is then the largest [[∞-groupoid]] contained in <math>C</math>. The core of ''C'' is also often written as <math>C^{\simeq}</math>. The left adjoint to the above inclusion is given by a [[localization of an ∞-category]].

In ''Kerodon'', the subcategory of a [[2-category]] ''C'' obtained by removing non-invertible morphisms is called the '''pith''' of ''C''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Construction 2.2.8.9 (The Pith of a 2-Category).  |url=https://kerodon.net/tag/00AL |website=Kerodon}}</ref> It can also be defined for an [[(∞, 2)-category]] ''C'';<ref>{{Cite web |title=5.4.5 The Pith of an (∞,2)-Category  |url=https://kerodon.net/tag/01XA |website=Kerodon}}</ref> namely, the pith of ''C'' is the largest simplicial subset that does not contain [[thin 2-simplex|non-thin 2-simplexes]].
